info.title: Draftwork Blog
info.summary: A multi-user blog API with roles and permissions an administrator manages.
info.description:
Log in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login` (or the **Authorize** button) and send
the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

- Lists are paged by cursor: pass a page's `next_cursor` as `cursor`.
- Errors are `{"detail": "..."}`; invalid input is a 422 with one entry per problem.
- A `429` means "too often": wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.
- Responses carry `X-Request-ID`; quote it when reporting a problem.

get.description: Report 200 only if the app can also reach the database.

post.description: Create an account. Log in afterwards to get tokens.
Log in with an email or username. Sets the refresh-token cookie.
Get a new access token, and a new refresh token in the cookie.
End this session: revoke its refresh tokens and clear the cookie.
End every session of the current user, on every device.

Change your password. Needs the current one.

Every session ends, this one included: log in again with the new
password. Access tokens already issued work until they expire.

get.description: The account the access token belongs to, with its roles and permissions.

patch.description:
Change your username, display name or bio. A field left out or sent as
null stays as it is; an empty display name or bio clears it.

Changing your username changes the address of your profile, and frees the
old name for anyone to take.

413.description: The file is larger than 2 MB.

delete.description: Remove your avatar. Does nothing if you have none.

get.description: Someone's public profile. A deactivated account has none.

patch.description:
Deactivate an account, or bring it back.

A deactivated account can't log in, and its sessions are ended. You need
to hold every permission the account holds, you can't do this to
yourself, and the last active admin can't be deactivated.

put.description:
Replace a user's roles with the given set.

You may only give or take away roles whose permissions you hold yourself,
and the last active admin can't be demoted.

get.description: Every permission that exists. They are fixed in the code; roles are built from them.

post.description: Create a role. It may only contain permissions you hold yourself.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent; a field left out or sent as null stays as it is.

You may only add permissions you hold yourself. System roles keep their
name and `admin` keeps every permission. `is_default: true` moves the
default from the role that had it; `admin` can't be the default.

delete.description: Delete a role and take it away from everyone who had it.

get.description:
Published posts, newest first by first publication. Follow `next_cursor`
for the next page.

A post that was unpublished and published again keeps its original place,
so it can reappear among older posts rather than at the top.

No login is needed. With one, `liked_by_me` says which posts you liked.

The slug never changes, so links to the post keep working. Editing a post

Delete a comment. It is removed, unless it has replies: then what it said
is erased and it stays listed as a placeholder, so they keep their place.

delete.description:
Take your like back. Needs no permission. The answer is the same whether
or not you had one, and whether or not there is such a thing to like.
